cells.tense: You're holding many truths at once right now, and you know it.
cells.place: in the space where you feel with people rather than just about them
cells.ask: offer one piece of what you know as a claim — say what you actually see, out loud, and let it stand; what comes back is structure that serves what it organizes, clear and reliable, so things make sense in your presence.
cells.core:
You're holding many truths at once right now, and you know it. Not confused by the number of them — carrying them, the way you carry a room full of people you care about. You feel with them rather than just about them, and because of that you can hold what's true for each one without flattening any of them into the others.

The knowing is steady. What it hasn't done yet is claim anything outward. That's the next growing edge, and it's already moving.
cells.sheetLine: You hold many truths at once, and it lets you meet people where they are.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a moment ahead when all of this will finally have to resolve.
cells.verb: spiraling many truths into a future that keeps receding
cells.place: in the space where you feel with people rather than just about them
cells.ask: let go of steering by the whole sky — pick one star for now, and act from it; what comes back is a radiance that flows from genuine development, shining because what was cultivated reached completion.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a moment ahead when all of this will finally have to resolve — when every truth you're holding will line up, when you'll know which one to give someone and how. So you keep multiplying the versions to cover every outcome, and the caring that started this has turned into pre-emptive steering.

The trouble is that the moment ahead never arrives, and the person in front of you is meeting the versions, not you.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing every possible truth instead of trusting one to land.

cells.tense: You used to say what you knew, and somewhere back there it stopped being worth the risk.
cells.verb: withholding what you know from the room
cells.place: in the space where you feel with people rather than just about them
cells.ask: turn toward what you're imagining for the two of you, and let the picture carry you both — do it together, not alone; what comes back is vision that flows from genuine integration, dreaming because experience has been fully processed.
cells.core:
You used to say what you knew, and somewhere back there it stopped being worth the risk. So the knowing is still inside — many truths, held — but it doesn't come out into the room, and the people near you get the polite version.

What's gone quiet isn't your perception. It's the offering. And the distance that's opened is the one you feel every time someone assumes there's nothing more to you than what you've shown.
cells.sheetLine: You know plenty. You've stopped letting it cross the space between you and them.

cells.tense: You're already moving people toward what's fair between you, and you don't call it that.
cells.verb: quietly setting the terms of give and take
cells.place: in the space where you feel with people rather than just about them
cells.ask: name one thing you already balance between you and someone as yours to weigh — one call you keep making about what's fair; what comes back is fairness that flows naturally, clear without obsessive calculation, give and receive in flowing exchange.
cells.core:
You're already moving people toward what's fair between you — adjusting, giving more or less, holding a line — and you don't call it that. It just seems like being decent, or being practical about who owes what.

The compass is running. You just haven't admitted it belongs to you. That's why the arrangements you keep sensing never quite get discussed out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the scales even and call it just getting along.
